rows.jp: アンテナは、破壊されていた。

rows.en: For an instant, I doubted my eyes.

ghs.en: For a moment I couldn't believe my eyes.

rows.jp: 先輩があんなに一生懸命組み立てていたものが。
rows.en: Something Misato had worked so hard to assemble.

ghs.en: That thing that Senpai had put together with all her strength...

ghs.assessment: 一瞬で means that the object was destroyed in an instant. 'For a moment' describes duration and loses the speed of destruction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'In an instant.'

highlights.text: For a moment.

rows.jp: すぐに思考の一部が、感情から離脱する。
rows.en: At once, part of my mind detached itself from my emotions.

ghs.en: Immediately afterwards a thought split off from emotions,

rows.jp: 冷静な思考に浸るために。

ghs.en: so that I could indulge in that one thought calmly:

rows.jp: 世界には８人しかいない。
rows.en: There were only eight people in the world.

ghs.en: In the world there are no more than 8 people.

rows.jp: 彼女は破壊された尖塔の足下にいた。
rows.en: She stood at the foot of the ruined spire.

ghs.en: She was standing underfoot the wrecked spire.
ghs.assessment: 尖塔の足下 means at the foot of the ruined spire. 'Standing underfoot the spire' reverses the spatial relation and is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She stood at the foot of the ruined spire.'

highlights.text: She was standing underfoot the wrecked spire.

rows.jp: 肩に触れるはずだった手が空を切る。
rows.en: The hand that should have touched her shoulder cut through empty air.

ghs.en: My hand that expected to touch a shoulder cuts empty air.
ghs.assessment: The narrator's hand, which was about to touch her shoulder, meets empty air. The English makes the hand 'expect' the touch and uses an indefinite shoulder.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The hand I meant to place on her shoulder cuts through empty air.'

highlights.text: My hand that expected to touch a shoulder cuts empty air.

rows.jp: 押し出すように言った。

ghs.en: Words that felt like they were shoving me away.
ghs.assessment: The source says she forces or pushes the words out. The English instead makes the words themselves feel as if they are shoving the narrator away, adding him as an object.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She forces the words out.'

highlights.text: Words that felt like they were shoving me away.

ghs.assessment: 胸 is the narrator's chest or heart in this moment, and the narration is past tense. 'The heart creaks' makes it generic and shifts tense.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My heart creaked.'

highlights.text: The heart creaks,

rows.jp: イントネーションにこめられた真意が、垣間見えたから。
rows.en: Because I had caught a glimpse of what that intonation really meant.

ghs.en: because I could glimpse the true intent loaded in her intonation.

rows.jp: 連れだって、二人がきた。
rows.en: The two of them arrived together.

rows.jp: 三人の視線が、先輩に向く。
rows.en: All three of us looked at Misato.

ghs.assessment: 視線 means the three people's gazes. 'Sightlines' is a technical spatial term rather than their act of looking.
ghs.remedy: Use 'All three gazes turn toward Senpai.'

highlights.text: Three sightlines turn to Senpai.

rows.jp: 「……私なわけないじゃないですか」

ghs.en: Misato: "...it cannot be me can it now?"
ghs.assessment: The denial requires normal interrogative punctuation and word order. 'It cannot be me can it now' is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It couldn't have been me, could it?'

highlights.text: Misato: "...it cannot be me can it now?"

rows.en: Her voice trembled as she answered.

ghs.en: So she answered in a shaking voice.

rows.jp: 「……自分で作って、自分で壊す人がいるわけないでしょう？」
rows.en: “Who would build something and then destroy it themselves?”

ghs.en: Misato: "...there are no people who would build something themselves, then tear it down themselves you know?"
ghs.assessment: The source's rhetorical question ends with でしょう. Appending 'you know' adds a conversational tag and produces clumsy English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'No one would build something themselves and then destroy it, would they?'

highlights.text: Misato: "...there are no people who would build something themselves, then tear it down themselves you know?"

ghs.en: There would have been people that act like that,
ghs.assessment: The source concedes that people like that did exist. 'There would have been people that act' mixes a past conditional with present tense.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There were people like that, though.'

highlights.text: There would have been people that act like that,

rows.jp: 人類が生存していた頃は。
rows.en: Back when humanity was still alive.

ghs.en: at the time when humanity was still in existence.

ghs.assessment: いや？ marks a reconsideration: 'Wait?' or 'Or...?' 'Well then?' instead advances the discussion and loses the self-correction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Wait.'

highlights.text: Well then?

ghs.en: Did Senpai wreck this by herself?

ghs.assessment: 可能性はあるのか is a question about whether the possibility exists. 'That possibility seems to exist' changes it into an assertion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Is that possible?'

highlights.text: That possibility seems to exist.

rows.jp: 「……姉貴、自分で壊したんじゃないのか？」

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...Aneki, you tore this down by yourself didn't you?"

rows.jp: 「完成したら、逃避先がなくなるから」
rows.en: “Because once it was finished, you’d have nowhere left to escape to.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Because once it's completed, there's nowhere ahead to escape to."
ghs.assessment: 逃避先 is a refuge or place to escape to. 'Nowhere ahead' adds a directional idea absent from the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Because once it was finished, you'd have nowhere left to escape to.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because once it's completed, there's nowhere ahead to escape to."

rows.en: “So you could reset everything to zero again.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "So you did this to return everything to 0 yourself."

rows.jp: そういうこともあり得る。

ghs.en: That is something that can be.
ghs.assessment: あり得る means that such a thing is possible. 'Something that can be' is an unnatural nominal calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That is possible.'

highlights.text: That is something that can be.

rows.jp: 特に先輩は。群青の人間だから。
rows.en: Especially for Misato. She was one of Gunjo’s people.

ghs.en: Especially with Senpai. Because she's one of the ultramarines of Gunjou.
ghs.assessment: 群青の人間 identifies her as a person of Gunjō, the established institution. 'One of the ultramarines of Gunjou' mistakes the proper institutional shorthand for the color noun and uses nonstandard romanization.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Especially Senpai, since she's one of Gunjō's.'

highlights.text: Especially with Senpai. Because she's one of the ultramarines of Gunjou.

rows.jp: 「逃げるために、逃げ道を作ったんだ」
rows.en: “You made yourself an escape route so you could run away.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "You created a way to escape so that you could still escape."

rows.jp: 「ちょっと待って。いくらなんでもそんな……」

ghs.en: Misato: "Wait a second! Things might be somewhat like that but this..."
ghs.assessment: いくらなんでもそんな rejects the accusation as going too far. 'Things might be somewhat like that but this' partially concedes it and is not grammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Wait. Even so, that's going too far...'

highlights.text: Misato: "Wait a second! Things might be somewhat like that but this..."

ghs.assessment: 三馬鹿 is simply 'the three idiots.' 'The Three Stooges' imports a specific American comedy allusion absent from the Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Use '...ugh, the three idiots.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...yuck, the three stooges."

rows.jp: 反応がないのを奇異に感じたのか、冬子は近づいてきた。
rows.en: Finding our lack of reaction strange, Kirihara came closer.

ghs.en: Probably feeling that the lack of a reaction was strange, Touko came closer.

rows.jp: 「支倉先輩が……話あるって矢文を……」
rows.en: “Hasekura sent me an arrow message... said she wanted to talk...”

ghs.en: Touko: "Hasekura-senpai sent me a letter attached to an arrow, saying she needs to... talk to me."

rows.jp: 破壊されたアンテナを見あげる。
rows.en: She looked up at the destroyed antenna.

ghs.en: She looks up at the wrecked antenna.

ghs.assessment: The passive 壊された states that someone deliberately destroyed it. 'It's been broken' can describe an accidental state and weakens the agentive contrast.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Someone destroyed it.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's been broken."

ghs.en: Tomoki: "By someone who is here right now."
The gap between Touko's eyebrows grows tighter.
ghs.assessment: 眉根が寄る means her brows knit. 'The gap between her eyebrows grows tighter' awkwardly describes geometry rather than the expression.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko's brows knit.'

highlights.text: The gap between Touko's eyebrows grows tighter.

ghs.assessment: それって introduces an unfinished inference: 'You mean...' 'But then' supplies an adversative transition not present in the source.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You mean...'

highlights.text: Touko: "But then..."

rows.jp: 「あまり愉快な話じゃないよな」
rows.en: “Not exactly a pleasant subject, is it?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's not a really pleasant story at all."

rows.jp: 「そうですよ、愉快なわけない……自分で壊すなんて……ありえない……」
rows.en: “No, it isn’t pleasant... Destroying it myself... impossible...”

ghs.en: Misato: "It is not, not pleasant at all... that I would have broken it... cannot be..."
ghs.assessment: The fragmented Japanese remains a first-person denial that she could have destroyed it herself. The English's 'that I would have broken it ... cannot be' is grammatically broken and obscures the denied action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Of course it isn't pleasant... But there's no way I destroyed it myself...'

highlights.text: Misato: "It is not, not pleasant at all... that I would have broken it... cannot be..."

ghs.assessment: 絶対、違います is an emphatic denial: 'It absolutely wasn't me' or 'That's absolutely wrong.' 'It is absolutely mistaken' sounds like an abstract classification and weakens the personal denial.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It absolutely wasn't me.'

highlights.text: Misato: "It is... absolutely mistaken."

rows.en: She began muttering under her breath.

rows.jp: 「このアンテナな、もとは放送部の活動用だったけど……救援信号を出すために使う予定だったんだよ」
rows.en: “This antenna was originally for the broadcasting club, but... we were going to use it to send a distress signal.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "This antenna was originally intended just for the Broadcast Club activities... but we were planning to use it to send an SOS signal."

ghs.assessment: そうでしょう seeks confirmation of the assertion just made: 'That's right, isn't it?' 'Is that right?' instead presents the speaker as unsure of the fact.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's right, isn't it, Senpai?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Is that right, Senpai?"

rows.jp: 話を向けられて、少し戸惑う先輩。
rows.en: Misato seemed a little thrown when I turned the conversation to her.

ghs.en: When the conversation turns towards her, Senpai grows a little bewildered.

rows.jp: 「そういう意図もありました」
「それが先輩にとっての部活動だった」
rows.en: “That was what club activity meant to you.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "These were club activities as far as Senpai is concerned."
ghs.assessment: それ is the singular project or activity and the source describes what it was for Senpai. 'These were club activities' changes both number and aspect.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That was Senpai's club activity.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "These were club activities as far as Senpai is concerned."

rows.jp: 「あながち逃避とも言えない。先があるからな」
rows.en: “It wasn’t mere escapism, either. It was leading somewhere.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It can't be said it was entirely flight. Because there's also a destination."
ghs.assessment: 先がある says the activity has a future or something beyond the present. 'There is also a destination' turns that temporal possibility into a physical endpoint.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You can't simply call it escapism. It was aimed at a future.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "It can't be said it was entirely flight. Because there's also a destination."

rows.jp: 「だから先輩のことを、俺は全然疑ってません」
rows.en: “So I don’t suspect you at all.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Therefore, I have no suspicions whatsoever regarding you, Senpai."

rows.en: “Try not to torture yourself over it.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Do not concern yourself too much about this."
ghs.assessment: 思い詰める means to brood, become obsessed, or work oneself into a state. 'Concern yourself' is much milder and misses that escalation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Don't brood over it too much.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Do not concern yourself too much about this."

rows.jp: 「ちょっと、なにどさくさにまぎれて耳触ってるのよ！」
rows.en: “Hey! Why are you touching her ear in the middle of all this?!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Wait, what are you whispering niceties in her ears under the cover of all this confusion!"
ghs.assessment: 耳触ってる explicitly accuses him of touching her ear. 'Whispering niceties in her ears' replaces the physical act with speech and invents its content.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Hey! Why are you taking advantage of the confusion to touch her ear?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Wait, what are you whispering niceties in her ears under the cover of all this confusion!"

rows.jp: 「こうすると落ち着くんだよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "To make her calm down of course."
ghs.assessment: The source states that doing this calms her. 'To make her calm down of course' recasts it as a purpose phrase and adds 'of course.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'This calms her down.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "To make her calm down of course."

rows.jp: 「そういうのは恋人同士でやることでしょう！」

ghs.en: Touko: "That's something that lovers would do you know!"

rows.jp: 「ふふふ、俺と先輩はいわば魂の恋人ソウルフルラブラバーなのだ」
rows.en: “Heh heh. Misato and I are, so to speak, soulmates—soulful love lovers.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hoh hoh hoh, me and Senpai are what you would call Lovers of the Soul ~ Soul Rubber(s)!"

rows.jp: 誰も笑わなかったし、ツッコミもなかった。
rows.en: No one laughed. No one even played the straight man.

ghs.en: No one laughed, and there was no straight man retort either.
I send eye signals to Touko.
ghs.assessment: 目線を送る means to give or shoot Tōko a meaningful look. 'Send eye signals' is an unnatural technical calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I shoot Tōko a look.'

highlights.text: I send eye signals to Touko.

rows.jp: 「……え？　なに？　ウインクなんてしてどうしたの？」
rows.en: “...What? Why are you winking at me?”

ghs.en: Touko: "...eh? What? You're winking at me, what's wrong?"

rows.en: She was unbelievably slow on the uptake.

rows.jp: 「どうして怒られないといけないわけ……」
rows.en: “Why am I the one getting yelled at...?”

ghs.en: Touko: "What is it that you even have to get angry for now..."
ghs.assessment: Tōko asks why she has to be scolded. 'Why you have to get angry' changes the subject to Taichi and reframes the complaint as a question about his emotion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Why do I have to get yelled at...?'

highlights.text: Touko: "What is it that you even have to get angry for now..."

rows.jp: 「ＯＫ、犯人捜しはもうやめだ！　さってと皆の衆、こいつをチャチャッと修理すればＳＯＳでヒューマンドラマだぞ！」
rows.en: “Okay, enough hunting for the culprit! All right, people—patch this thing up in a jiffy, send an SOS, and cue the human drama!”

ghs.assessment: The English translates only the opening decision to stop searching for the culprit. It omits the entire ensuing rally to repair the antenna quickly and produce an SOS human drama.
ghs.remedy: Restore the omitted second sentence.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Okay, culprit search stops here!"

rows.jp: 「必要な機材が燃やされています。修理はできません」
rows.en: “They burned the equipment we need. It cannot be repaired.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Necessary equipment has been burned. Repairs cannot be performed."

rows.en: She pointed to the equipment at our feet.

ghs.en: She points at equipment right to her underfoot.
ghs.assessment: 足下 means the equipment at her feet. 'Right to her underfoot' is ungrammatical and suggests that she is standing on it.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She points to the equipment at her feet.'

highlights.text: She points at equipment right to her underfoot.

rows.jp: 「ガソリンっぽい臭いがします。かけて、燃やしたんです」
rows.en: “It smells like gasoline. They poured it on and set it alight.”

ghs.en: Misato: "There is a smell like gasoline. It was doused then lit on fire."

rows.jp: そんな徹底してるとは。
rows.en: I hadn’t thought they’d be so thorough.

ghs.assessment: The source expresses shock that the destruction was so thorough. 'That thoroughness means...' is an unfinished English proposition and omits the reaction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I hadn't expected them to be so thorough.'

highlights.text: That thoroughness means...

rows.jp: 「ま、まあ犯人なんて追求しても仕方ないなーっと」
rows.en: “W-well, there’s no point chasing after the culprit anyway...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, weeell even if we go after whoever did this, it won't change, that's what it means."
ghs.assessment: 仕方ない says there is no point in pursuing the culprit. 'It won't change, that's what it means' supplies an unclear object and explanatory tag.
ghs.remedy: Use 'W-well, there's no point trying to hunt down the culprit.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Well, weeell even if we go after whoever did this, it won't change, that's what it means."

rows.jp: 「犯人が誰か、知りたいですね」
rows.en: “I want to know who did it.”

ghs.en: Misato: "I do want to know who was it that did this."
ghs.assessment: The embedded question requires 'who it was that did this,' not 'who was it that did this.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'I want to know who did this.'

highlights.text: Misato: "I do want to know who was it that did this."

rows.jp: 「少なくとも私じゃない。だとすれば、あなたたちの誰かじゃないですか」
rows.en: “At the very least, it wasn’t me. Which means it was one of you, doesn’t it?”

ghs.en: Misato: "At the very least it ain't me. So in other words, it is one of you people is it not?"
ghs.assessment: The English stacks 'in other words,' a declarative clause, and 'is it not' without grammatical agreement. The source is a pointed but coherent accusation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'At least it wasn't me. Which means it was one of you, doesn't it?'

highlights.text: Misato: "At the very least it ain't me. So in other words, it is one of you people is it not?"

rows.jp: 言葉は銃弾に似ている。
一度放てば、取り返しがきかない。
rows.en: Once fired, they cannot be taken back.

ghs.en: Once fired, there is no taking them back.
Whether they miss, whether they wound.

rows.jp: だが見里先輩の言葉は、ことによく理解に届いた。
rows.en: But Misato’s words hit home with unusual clarity.

ghs.en: But Misato-senpai's words well carried her understanding.
ghs.assessment: ことによく理解に届いた says Misato's words conveyed their meaning particularly clearly. 'Carried her understanding' reverses the relation and treats her understanding as the transported object.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But Misato-senpai's words got their meaning across with particular clarity.'

highlights.text: But Misato-senpai's words well carried her understanding.

rows.jp: 「あなたたちの誰かが裏切った」

ghs.en: Misato: "One of you people betrayed us."

rows.jp: 優しいはずの眼鏡の先輩だった。
rows.en: She was supposed to be the kind upperclassman in glasses.

ghs.en: This was the bespectacled Senpai one would expect to be kind.

rows.jp: 怒られることはあったけど。

ghs.en: There are times when she did get angry, however,

rows.jp: 告発されることはないと思っていた。
rows.en: But I never thought she would accuse me.

ghs.en: I never thought she would make accusations.

rows.jp: 「人を……裏切り者呼ばわりしてさぁ！」
rows.en: “You go and... call someone a traitor!”

rows.jp: 「あんたが、裏切りとか言うってことは―――」
rows.en: “If you’re the one talking about betrayal—”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "You of all people, saying even the word 'betrayal'---"

rows.jp: 桜庭が動いた瞬間、友貴が倒れた。
rows.en: The instant Sakuraba moved, Tomoki went down.

ghs.en: In the instant Sakuraba moved, Tomoki was struck down.
ghs.assessment: The source says Tomoki fell the instant Sakuraba moved. 'Was struck down' adds a completed attack mechanism before the narrator's following uncertainty.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The instant Sakuraba moved, Tomoki fell.'

highlights.text: In the instant Sakuraba moved, Tomoki was struck down.

ghs.assessment: 殴った？ is the narrator's question 'Did he hit him?' 'A punch?' removes both actor and target.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Did he hit him?'

highlights.text: A punch?

ghs.assessment: The source questions whether Sakuraba hit Tomoki. 'From Sakuraba to Tomoki?' is a prepositional fragment that does not state the action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Sakuraba hit Tomoki?'

highlights.text: From Sakuraba to Tomoki?

ghs.en: Taichi: "Come now, come now, come now, come now!"

rows.jp: 展開についていけない。

ghs.en: I can't keep up with the developments.

ghs.assessment: The interruption can distort the final words, but 'OwChCh, whass'at' is not a controlled or readily legible representation of the spoken line.
ghs.remedy: Use a legible interrupted complaint such as 'Ow... what was that for...?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "OwChCh, whass'at for..."

rows.jp: 言葉は友貴に向けられていた。
rows.en: The question was directed at Tomoki.

ghs.en: The words had been aimed at Tomoki.
Taichi: "Did you say he destroyed it?"

rows.jp: 「どうして壊す必要があったんだ」
rows.en: “Why did you need to destroy it?”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "Why did you even need to destroy it."
ghs.assessment: The English renders a direct question with a period.
ghs.remedy: End the line with a question mark.

highlights.text: Sakuraba: "Why did you even need to destroy it."

rows.jp: シリアスに桜庭は言う。

rows.en: “...What are you talking about? I don’t know anything.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "...what are you talking about. I don't know anything!"

rows.jp: 「おまえがアンテナを壊す瞬間を、見たんだ」
rows.en: “I saw the moment you destroyed the antenna.”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "The moment when you smashed the antenna, I saw it."

rows.jp: 友貴の口元が、不自然に歪んだその瞬間。
rows.en: Just as Tomoki’s mouth twisted unnaturally—

ghs.en: Tomoki's lips deformed unnaturally, and that very instant,

rows.jp: 音は甲高く、静寂に亀裂を入れた。
rows.en: Its high-pitched shriek cracked the silence.

ghs.en: The sound is a high-pitched shrill that forms cracks into the silence.
ghs.assessment: The source says the high-pitched sound cracks the silence. 'A high-pitched shrill' uses an adjective as a noun, while 'forms cracks into' is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The high-pitched sound cracked the silence.'

highlights.text: The sound is a high-pitched shrill that forms cracks into the silence.

ghs.assessment: 武装していた states that Kiri was armed. 'Had a weapon' reports possession but loses the deliberate state of being equipped for confrontation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kiri was armed.'

highlights.text: Kiri had a weapon.

rows.jp: 全員の動きが止まる。縫い止められた。

ghs.en: All stopped their movement. As if sewed into place.

rows.jp: 霧が手にするクロスボウ、そのこめられた矢によって。
rows.en: By the bolt loaded into Kiri’s crossbow.

ghs.en: Kiri's hands held a crossbow, and it was loaded with a bolt.

rows.jp: 「動けば撃ちます。これ玩具じゃありませんから」
rows.en: “Move and I’ll shoot. This isn’t a toy.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Move and I shoot. I warn you that this is not a toy."

rows.jp: バックマスター社製・マックスポイントクロスボー。

ghs.en: It's a Buckmaster Manufacture Maxpoint Crossbow.
ghs.assessment: The product construction is Buckmaster-made Maxpoint Crossbow. 'Buckmaster Manufacture' is not grammatical as either a manufacturer name or attribution.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A Buckmaster Maxpoint Crossbow.'

highlights.text: It's a Buckmaster Manufacture Maxpoint Crossbow.

rows.jp: オプションのコッキング装置がついている。
rows.en: It was fitted with the optional cocking device.

ghs.en: Crank cocking aid optional is installed.
ghs.assessment: The source says it has the optional cocking device fitted. 'Crank cocking aid optional is installed' has broken modifier order and no article.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It is fitted with the optional cocking device.'

highlights.text: Crank cocking aid optional is installed.

rows.jp: 女性仕様といったところか。

ghs.assessment: 女性仕様 means it is configured or outfitted for a woman. 'Woman spec' is an ungrammatical technical calque.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A configuration intended for a woman, perhaps.'

highlights.text: Is it woman spec then?

rows.jp: とはいえ狩猟用の強力な武器。癖のない使用感。十二分な殺傷力。
rows.en: Even so, it was a powerful hunting weapon. Easy to handle. More than lethal enough.

ghs.en: That said, it's still a powerful weapon for hunting. Seems usable even without training. More than enough killing power.
ghs.assessment: 癖のない使用感 means straightforward, predictable handling. 'Usable even without training' adds a claim about the user's training and changes the weapon characteristic.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even so, it is a powerful hunting weapon: straightforward to handle, with more than enough lethality.'

highlights.text: That said, it's still a powerful weapon for hunting. Seems usable even without training. More than enough killing power.

rows.jp: おそらく誰かの家屋にあったものだろう。
rows.en: She had probably found it in someone’s house.

ghs.en: It perhaps was in somebody's house, I guess.

rows.jp: にわか成金の多い街ならではの、無防備さで。
rows.en: The kind of carelessness peculiar to a town full of nouveau riche.

ghs.en: It is the defenselessness of a town characterized by many overnight millionaires.
Kiri: "Kurosu Taichi in particular will not move!"
ghs.assessment: The source is a forceful imperative directed especially at Kurosu Taichi. 'Will not move' changes the command into an awkward future declaration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kurosu Taichi, especially—do not move!'

highlights.text: Kiri: "Kurosu Taichi in particular will not move!"

rows.jp: 「わたしがもっとも、うっかり殺してしまいたい相手だから、あなたは」
rows.en: “Because you’re the one I most want to kill by accident.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because the one of you I would most extremely like to just accidentally kill would be you."

ghs.assessment: 冷笑する is a complete action by Kiri. 'Mocking smile' is a subjectless noun phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She sneers.'

highlights.text: Mocking smile.

ghs.assessment: おいおい is an incredulous 'Come on' or 'Hey, now.' The parenthetical 'dear dear' selects an unrelated address term.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Come on.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "......(dear dear)"

rows.jp: 「ちょっと、どういうことなの？　全然わからない？」
rows.en: “Wait, what is going on? I don’t understand any of this!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Really, what are you doing? I don't get this at all you know?"
ghs.assessment: どういうことなの asks what is going on or what this means. 'What are you doing?' changes it into an accusation about an action by the addressee.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Wait, what is going on? I don't understand any of this.'

highlights.text: Touko: "Really, what are you doing? I don't get this at all you know?"

rows.jp: 「佐倉もちょっと落ち着きなさいよ」
rows.en: “Sakura, you need to calm down too.”

ghs.en: Touko: "Calm down a little already, Sakura!"

rows.jp: 一歩踏み出しかけた冬子を、左に１５度スライドしたボウの先端が制した。
rows.en: Kirihara started forward, and the bow’s tip slid fifteen degrees left to stop her.

ghs.en: As soon as Touko takes half one step out, the pointed end of the bow turned to the left by 15 degrees and put her in check.
ghs.assessment: Tōko starts to take one step; the bow tip slides fifteen degrees left and checks her. 'Takes half one step out' is ungrammatical and changes the amount of movement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'As Tōko begins to step forward, the bow tip slides fifteen degrees left and stops her.'

highlights.text: As soon as Touko takes half one step out, the pointed end of the bow turned to the left by 15 degrees and put her in check.

rows.jp: 「ちょっと！　私は関係ないでしょ！」
rows.en: “Hey! I have nothing to do with this!”

ghs.en: Touko: "Really! I have nothing to do with this I don't!"
ghs.assessment: The duplicated negative 'I have nothing to do with this I don't' is not motivated by the Japanese.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Hey! I have nothing to do with this!'

highlights.text: Touko: "Really! I have nothing to do with this I don't!"

rows.jp: 全員に向けて、霧は甲高い声を張り上げる。
rows.en: Kiri raised her high voice to address everyone.

ghs.en: Kiri shouts at the top of her voice towards all of us.

rows.jp: 「上見坂市の団地坂から、市役所までのライン……ここが私たちの領土ってことです」
rows.en: “The area between Danchizaka in Kamimisaka City and city hall... That will be our territory.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "The borderline runs from the hill of the Kamisaka City Apartment Complex to the City Hall... therefore this is our possession."
ghs.assessment: The stated line marks a territorial boundary and defines the enclosed area as their territory. 'Possession' weakens and changes the political term repeated immediately afterward.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The line from the housing-complex hill in Kamisaka City to City Hall marks the boundary. Everything inside is our territory.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "The borderline runs from the hill of the Kamisaka City Apartment Complex to the City Hall... therefore this is our possession."

rows.jp: 「そこにある食料や水、衣類やその他の雑貨類も、当然こちら側のものってことです」
rows.en: “The food and water, clothes, and other sundries inside it will naturally belong to us as well.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "All the food and water that is there, clothes and other miscellaneous goods naturally belong to our side."

ghs.assessment: そうじゃありませんよ is a straightforward 'That's not what we're doing.' 'That it is not' is ungrammatical inversion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's not it.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "That it is not."

rows.jp: 「食料品やその他の店は、設定した国境の反対側にも存在しますから」
rows.en: “There are grocery stores and other shops on the far side of the border we’ve drawn too.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because grocery and miscellaneous stores do exist on the other side of the established national border."

rows.en: “Our side contains roughly thirty percent of them.”

rows.jp: 「妥当なのはわかった。けど理由は？」
rows.en: “I get that it’s fair. But why?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Appropriate, fine, I get it. But for what reason?"

rows.en: Kiri looked taken aback by the question.

ghs.assessment: 鼻白む says Kiri looks taken aback or put off by the question. 'Asking the question daunts Kiri' assigns agency to the question and changes the visible reaction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kiri looks put off by the question.'

highlights.text: Asking the question daunts Kiri.

rows.jp: 「あなたがたが信頼できないからです」

ghs.en: Kiri: "Because we cannot trust you people."

rows.jp: 「峰南町の向こう、坂井橋を越えた雑木林の中で……」
rows.en: “Beyond Hōnan, across Sakai Bridge, in a thicket...”

ghs.en: Kiri: "Heading through Hounan Ward, in a grove just past the Sakai Bridge..."
ghs.assessment: Standard Hepburn renders 峰南 as Hōnan. 'Hounan' uses nonstandard vowel spelling.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Hōnan.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "Heading through Hounan Ward, in a grove just past the Sakai Bridge..."

rows.en: A silent shock ran through us.

ghs.assessment: The source says a voiceless shock runs through the group. 'An impact runs through, voiceless' treats the shock as a physical impact and leaves its experiencers unstated.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A silent shock runs through us.'

highlights.text: An impact runs through, voiceless.

rows.jp: 「老人の死体でした。詳しくは確認してません」
rows.en: “An old man’s body. We didn’t examine it closely.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "It was the body of an older person. Details were not ascertained."

rows.jp: 簡潔な説明で質問を封じて、霧はさらに続けた。
rows.en: Kiri’s curt explanation cut off any questions, and she continued.

ghs.en: Sealing all questions with a concise explanation, Kiri pressed onwards.

rows.jp: 「犯人は……この中にいるとわたしは考えてます」
rows.en: “I believe... the culprit is one of you.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "The culprit is... among you, I conclude."
ghs.assessment: この中 means among everyone present, including the speaker's side. 'Among you' excludes Kiri and her companion and narrows the accusation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I believe the culprit is... among us.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "The culprit is... among you, I conclude."

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ain't that just an extraordinary story."
ghs.assessment: 突拍子もない calls the accusation outrageous or far-fetched. 'Extraordinary' can be neutral or admiring and misses the dismissal.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's a far-fetched story.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ain't that just an extraordinary story."

ghs.en: Kiri: "And you... are the most suspicious!"

rows.jp: 俺にクロスボウが向く。
今にも矢が飛び出しそうだ。
rows.en: The bolt looked ready to fly at any moment.

ghs.en: It felt that a bolt could fly out of it any moment.
ghs.assessment: The source directly says the bolt looks ready to fly at any moment. 'It felt that' adds an experiencer construction and shifts the immediate visual observation into past subjective report.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The bolt looks ready to fly at any moment.'

highlights.text: It felt that a bolt could fly out of it any moment.

rows.jp: 「前科のあるあなたが……一番の容疑者なんですよ！」
rows.en: “With your record... you’re the prime suspect!”

ghs.en: Kiri: "You have a previous offense... you are therefore suspect number one!"

ghs.assessment: 前科、か is a reflective 'A prior offense, huh.' 'A previous offense, have I' uses unsupported mock-archaic inversion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A prior offense, huh.'

highlights.text: A previous offense, have I.

rows.jp: 「他の人だって、可能性はあります」
rows.en: “Any of the others could have done it too.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "And it could be someone else, there is the possibility."
ghs.assessment: 'It could be someone else, there is the possibility' repeats the proposition in a comma splice. The Japanese is one direct qualification.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Someone else is also possible.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "And it could be someone else, there is the possibility."

rows.jp: 霧の隣、美希が小さく顔を伏せている。
rows.en: Beside Kiri, Miki lowered her face slightly.

ghs.en: Next to Kiri, Miki's face was looking down a little.
ghs.assessment: 美希が小さく顔を伏せている says Miki slightly lowers her face. 'Miki's face was looking down' makes the face itself the perceiving subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Beside Kiri, Miki lowers her face slightly.'

highlights.text: Next to Kiri, Miki's face was looking down a little.

rows.en: She showed no sign of speaking.

ghs.en: There's no indication that she will speak.

rows.jp: 早く終わってほしいと、ただ願っているような。
rows.en: As though she only wanted this to be over.

ghs.en: As if all she wanted was for this to be over soon.

rows.jp: 「あー、きみたちの言い分はよくわかった」
rows.en: “Okay, I think I understand your position.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh, I totally got what your point is."
ghs.assessment: The idiomatic acknowledgment is 'I understand your position.' 'I totally got what your point is' mixes tense and produces awkward colloquial emphasis.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I understand your position.'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Ahhh, I totally got what your point is."

rows.jp: 「だが我々は同じグループの仲間であり、人類最後の生き残りで―――」
rows.en: “But we’re all part of the same group, the last survivors of humanity—”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But all of us are in the same group of True Companions, the last survivors of mankind, and---"
ghs.assessment: 仲間 means companions or members of the same group. Capitalized 'True Companions' invents a special doctrinal label.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But we belong to the same group; we are companions and humanity's last survivors—'

highlights.text: Taichi: "But all of us are in the same group of True Companions, the last survivors of mankind, and---"

rows.jp: 霧の言葉が、切り裂いた。
rows.en: Kiri’s words cut straight through mine.

ghs.en: Kiri's words tore me to shreds.
ghs.assessment: Kiri's next words cut through the narrator's unfinished speech. 'Tore me to shreds' changes the object from his words to his person and greatly increases the force.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Kiri's words cut across mine.'

highlights.text: Kiri's words tore me to shreds.

rows.jp: 「仲間だと思ったことは、一度たりともない」
rows.en: “I have never once considered you my friends.”

ghs.en: Kiri: "I never thought we were close friends, not even once."
ghs.assessment: 仲間 is a companion or member of the group, not specifically a close friend. The English narrows the rejected relationship.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I have never once thought of you as companions.'

highlights.text: Kiri: "I never thought we were close friends, not even once."

rows.jp: シン、と屋上は冷え切った。
「まあ、いい機会なんじゃないかな」

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Well, isn't this a nice opportunity then."

ghs.assessment: ひどく冷静 describes the words as terribly or chillingly calm. 'Calculated' instead attributes strategic design.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Terribly calm words.'

highlights.text: Horribly calculated words.

rows.jp: 「どうせさ、何したってうまく行くはずもないんだし」
rows.en: “Nothing we do is ever going to work out anyway.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Because whatever we did, I never expected things to go well."
ghs.assessment: The source says that whatever they do cannot possibly go well. 'I never expected' adds the speaker's prior mental state and shifts the general claim into past expectation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Nothing we do is going to work anyway.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Because whatever we did, I never expected things to go well."

rows.jp: 「僕もこの人と仲良くなんて、考えたくもないし」
rows.en: “And I don’t even want to think about getting along with her.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "I never even wanted to think of being on good terms with this guy here either."
ghs.assessment: この人 refers to the woman under discussion. 'This guy' misgenders the referent and changes the interpersonal target.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I don't even want to consider getting along with her.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "I never even wanted to think of being on good terms with this guy here either."

ghs.en: Taichi: "Were you the one who broke the antenna?"

rows.jp: 「姉貴が逃げるのが、許せなかった」
rows.en: “I couldn’t forgive sis for running away.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Aneki was running away, that can't be allowed."
ghs.assessment: Tomoki says he could not forgive his sister for escaping. 'That can't be allowed' removes him as experiencer and changes past motive into a present rule.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I couldn't forgive my sister for running away.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "Aneki was running away, that can't be allowed."

rows.jp: 「人の逃げ場を奪っておいて、自分だけ逃げるのかって」
rows.en: “She’d taken away someone else’s escape—then she was going to run away on her own?”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "If she steals refuges from others, she can be only one to run away, that's what she thinks."
ghs.assessment: Tomoki accuses his sister: after taking away other people's refuges, was she going to escape alone? The English switches to third person and then says 'that's what she thinks,' reversing the utterance.
ghs.remedy: Use 'After taking away everyone else's refuge, you were going to escape by yourself?'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "If she steals refuges from others, she can be only one to run away, that's what she thinks."

rows.jp: 「人に厳しいなら、自分にも厳しくしないとな」
rows.en: “If you’re hard on other people, you have to be hard on yourself too.”

ghs.en: Tomoki: "If you're strict with others, then be strict with yourself too, 'K."
ghs.assessment: The source ends the maxim normally. The appended ''K' is an unexplained English addition.
ghs.remedy: Remove ''K.'

highlights.text: Tomoki: "If you're strict with others, then be strict with yourself too, 'K."

rows.jp: 親しげに語りかけるようでもある。
rows.en: Almost as if speaking to her affectionately.

ghs.en: but also spoken as if they were amicable.

rows.jp: 「独立。いいんじゃないかな、佐倉」

ghs.en: Tomoki: "Independence. That's fine with me, Sakura."

rows.jp: 「……あなたたちは、信頼できない」

rows.en: “Is everyone really all right with this?”

ghs.en: Sakuraba: "We all OK with this, everyone?"

rows.en: The seven of us as we had been.

ghs.assessment: 七人の平常 means the seven people's ordinary state or normality. 'The usual of seven people' is not grammatical English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The seven of us, as usual.'

highlights.text: The usual of seven people.

rows.en: Something that should already have been lost.

ghs.en: It's something that should have been lost.

rows.jp: 友情の残骸でしかなかったそれも、今、完全に破壊されて。
rows.en: It had been nothing but the wreckage of friendship; now even that was utterly destroyed.

ghs.en: What was never anything more than the wreckage of friendships is, now, being completely destroyed.

ghs.assessment: 断絶 is severance or rupture. 'Disintegration' suggests gradual physical decomposition and misses the interpersonal break.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A break. Or a severance.'

highlights.text: Breakdown. Or disintegration.

rows.jp: それは最初からあって、ただ、見えなかっただけなのだ。
rows.en: It had been there from the start. We simply hadn’t been able to see it.

ghs.en: It was there from the start, just, it was merely not seen.

rows.jp: 友達の演技を、ひとりひとりがしていたのだとしたら。
rows.en: If, one by one, we had all been pretending to be friends.

ghs.en: If every single one of us was acting in the role of friend then...

ghs.assessment: 違った is an immediate self-correction: 'No' or 'That's not it.' 'It was wrong' shifts it into a past evaluative claim.
ghs.remedy: Use 'No.'

highlights.text: It was wrong.

rows.jp: こんなことを、夢想していたのではなかった。
rows.en: This was not what I had dreamed of.

ghs.en:
This, what I was seeing,
was never my vision.
ghs.assessment: The narrator says this is not what he had dreamed or imagined. 'What I was seeing' changes remembered desire into present perception.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This wasn't what I had dreamed of.'

highlights.text:
This, what I was seeing,
was never my vision.

rows.jp: 俺がほんのりと期待していたのは。
rows.en: What I had dimly hoped for was—

ghs.en:
What I was merely
faintly expecting was,

ghs.assessment: The repeated 違う continues the immediate correction, 'No.' 'Mistaken' is a predicate fragment with no clear subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'No.'

highlights.text: mistaken.

rows.jp: 他愛ない部活動でよかった。
rows.en: Some silly club activity would have been enough.

ghs.en:
Just those silly innocent afterschool
activities, those I wanted.

rows.jp: どこで間違えたのだろう。

ghs.en: Where was the mistake made, even.
ghs.assessment: The narrator asks where he went wrong. 'Where was the mistake made' removes his agency and turns it into an abstract error.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Where did I go wrong?'

highlights.text: Where was the mistake made, even.

rows.jp: そもそもにして、全てが壮大な間違いだったとも思える。
rows.en: Or perhaps everything had been a monumental mistake from the very beginning.

ghs.en:
I think that, from the very beginning,
everything had been one majestic and
wonderful mistake.
ghs.assessment: 壮大 means grand or colossal in scale. 'Wonderful' adds positive admiration absent from the bitter self-indictment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Maybe everything was one colossal mistake from the very beginning.'

highlights.text:
I think that, from the very beginning,
everything had been one majestic and
wonderful mistake.

ghs.assessment: 群青 is the established shorthand for Gunjō Academy. 'Gunjou' is nonstandard romanization and omits the institution type.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The school called Gunjō Academy.'

highlights.text: The school known as Gunjou.

rows.jp: 田崎商店という雑貨屋。

ghs.en: The grocery store known as Tasaki.
ghs.assessment: 雑貨屋 is a general store, not specifically a grocery store. The English narrows the business type.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The general store called Tasaki Store.'

highlights.text: The grocery store known as Tasaki.

ghs.en: The omnipotence known as the world.

ghs.assessment: The source metadata and following narration identify this as Taichi's spoken line. The English omits the speaker label used throughout the script.
ghs.remedy: Attribute the line to Taichi.

highlights.text: "Gone mad."

ghs.assessment: 小さく modifies the act as quiet or soft. 'Tiny muttering' incorrectly makes the utterance physically small.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I muttered softly.'

highlights.text: That was my tiny muttering.

rows.jp: 黒いシルエットに支配される視界。
rows.en: Black silhouettes took possession of my vision.

ghs.en:
Dark black silhouettes
dominate my field of vision.
ghs.assessment: 黒い already means black, so 'dark black' is redundant. The source presents a field of vision ruled by black silhouette, while the English pluralizes the image.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My vision is dominated by black silhouettes.'

highlights.text:
Dark black silhouettes
dominate my field of vision.

rows.jp: 影法師たちが言い争っている。

ghs.en: I want to make it end.
I want to make it all end.

rows.jp: 残滓(ざんし)でしかない今でさえ、耐え難い苦痛だった。
rows.en: Even now, when all that remained was residue, it was unbearable agony.

ghs.en:
Even if all that remains now are
dregs, the agony was unbearable.
ghs.assessment: The source states that even the present, now nothing but residue, was unbearable pain. 'Even if' makes that state hypothetical, and 'all that remains are dregs' changes the grammatical relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even this present, nothing but residue, was unbearable agony.'

highlights.text:
Even if all that remains now are
dregs, the agony was unbearable.

rows.jp: 人が滅んで、人との摩擦がなくなったと思った。
rows.en: Humanity was gone. I thought the friction between people had vanished with it.

ghs.en:
Once people were gone, I thought,
the friction between people would be
no more.

rows.jp: けどこの有様はどうだ。

ghs.en: Then how can things be like this.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is a complete, incredulous question about the present state of affairs. The English is punctuated as a statement and uses an awkward interrogative construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'But look at what has happened.' or 'Then how did things come to this?'

highlights.text: Then how can things be like this.

ghs.en: no more than eight people, and,

rows.en: And still we fought and hated one another?

ghs.assessment: The source asks whether even eight people will fight and hate one another. 'Perhaps reciprocal hate' turns the questioned action into a tentative noun phrase and breaks the parallel construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And even with only eight people, we fight and hate one another?'

highlights.text: there's conflict, perhaps reciprocal hate.

ghs.assessment: そうか marks dawning recognition here: 'I see.' 'Of course' instead presents the conclusion as obvious or expected.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I see.'

highlights.text: Of course.

rows.jp: ひとりじゃないと駄目なんだ。
rows.en: It had to be one person alone.

ghs.en:
all is pointless if
you're not alone.
ghs.assessment: ひとりじゃないと駄目なんだ says that being alone is necessary. 'All is pointless' introduces a claim about futility rather than stating that condition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It has to be one person alone.'

highlights.text:
all is pointless if
you're not alone.

rows.en: There could not be more than one.

rows.jp: 個でなければ、人は人のまま。
rows.en: Unless each stood alone, people remained people.

ghs.en:
If one is not Individual,
the person stays a person.

rows.en: How to make each one stand alone?

ghs.assessment: 個にするには asks how to make the people under consideration into individuals. 'Individual, but to become one' is not a grammatical question and changes the implied object into a singular speaker.
ghs.remedy: Use 'How can they be made individual?'

highlights.text: Individual, but to become one...?

ghs.assessment: あいつ is a hostile third-person pronoun in the command to kill its referent. 'That one' is an unnatural demonstrative calque in English dialogue.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Kill them! Kill them!' with the contextually established pronoun.

highlights.text: Miki: "...kill, kill that one!"

rows.jp: 美希が叫ぶ。もうどうでもいい。
rows.en: Miki screamed. I no longer cared.

ghs.en: Miki is shouting. I don't care anymore.

ghs.assessment: The source repeats the urgent command to kill the same target. The English leaves out the action entirely and retains only the calqued object 'that one.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Hurry—hurry, kill them!' with the contextually established pronoun.

highlights.text: Miki: "Hurry, hurry, that one!"

rows.jp: ……どうでもいい。殺し合えばいい。
rows.en: ...I didn’t care. Let them kill each other.

ghs.en: ...I don't care anymore. Killing each other is fine.

ghs.assessment: なんだったかな is a recollective question, 'What was it again?' 'What was even this' is ungrammatical and changes recollection into a judgment about the present thing.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What was it again?'

highlights.text: What was even this.

ghs.assessment: The source simply repeats that it is a kind world. 'I say' adds a speech-reporting tag that is not present and makes the fragment sound defensive.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A kind world.'

highlights.text: A kind world, I say.

rows.jp: 俺のような人間モドキでも生きていける、慈愛に満ちあふれた世界。
rows.en: A world overflowing with compassion, where even a counterfeit human like me could live.

ghs.en: It's a world filled to overflowing with compassion, where even a praying mantis dressed up as a human like me can be allowed to live.
ghs.assessment: 人間モドキ means a pseudo-human or imitation human. The English invents a praying mantis dressed as a human, replacing the source image with an unrelated creature and costume.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A world overflowing with compassion, where even a pseudo-human like me is allowed to live.'

highlights.text: It's a world filled to overflowing with compassion, where even a praying mantis dressed up as a human like me can be allowed to live.

ghs.assessment: どうやって asks by what means the stated realization is to be achieved. 'What do I do?' changes the question from method to a first-person course of action.
ghs.remedy: Use '...How?'

highlights.text: ...what do I do?

ghs.assessment: 決まっている means that the answer is already obvious or settled. 'That is certain' instead affirms the truth of an unspecified proposition.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The answer is obvious.'

highlights.text: That is certain.

rows.jp: 世界には動か静しかない。
rows.en: There was only motion or stillness in the world.

ghs.en: in this world of motion or stillness nothing else,
ghs.assessment: The source says the world contains only motion or stillness. 'In this world of motion or stillness nothing else' is not a grammatical English proposition and obscures the exhaustive contrast.
ghs.remedy: Use 'In this world, there is only motion and stillness.'

highlights.text: in this world of motion or stillness nothing else,

ghs.assessment: 動を静にする is the abstract operation of turning motion into stillness. The English adds a first-person subject and uses the unnatural count noun 'the motion.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Turn motion into stillness.'

highlights.text: I make the motion still.

rows.jp: そういう思考が、確かにあった。
rows.en: That thought had unmistakably been there.

ghs.en: I was thinking that, I definitely was.

rows.jp: 知らずに歩き始めていたのかも知れない。
rows.en: Perhaps I had begun walking without even knowing it.

ghs.en: I may have started walking without realizing, maybe.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese expresses uncertainty once. 'May have ... maybe' duplicates the same hedge and produces awkward English.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Perhaps I had started walking without realizing it.'

highlights.text: I may have started walking without realizing, maybe.

rows.en: I could not make it out.

ghs.en: Cannot understand what is being said.
ghs.assessment: 聞き取れない is a complete first-person perception: the voice cannot be made out. 'Cannot understand' is a subjectless English fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can't make out the words.'

highlights.text: Cannot understand what is being said.

rows.en: I did not even know who it was.

ghs.en: Even just the who is incomprehensible.
ghs.assessment: 誰かさえわからない means that the narrator cannot even tell who is speaking. 'Even just the who is incomprehensible' turns the interrogative into an ungrammatical noun phrase.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can't even tell who it is.'

highlights.text: Even just the who is incomprehensible.
